findings.evidence: grep shows no `coord_symm` lemma; only `coord_basis_zero`/`coord_basis_one` (lines 386-392). Docstring line 428 advertises `p · μ + q · λ` but nothing derives it.
findings.fix: Add `coord_symm_apply : T.coord.symm (p, q) = p • T.basis 0 + q • T.basis 1` (or a `slopeEquiv_symm_apply_coe` giving `Slope.mk (r.num • T.basis 0 + r.den • T.basis 1) _`) so the inverse parametrisation is usable without unfolding.
findings.issue: The inverse of the framed parametrisation cannot express the filling class `p·μ + q·λ` through the API. `slopeEquiv_symm_apply` leaves `Slope.congr T.coord.symm (slopeOfValue x)` opaque, and `coord` is only characterized forward (`coord_basis_zero/one`); there is no lemma giving `T.coord.symm (p, q) = p • T.basis 0 + q • T.basis 1`, so the `p·μ + q·λ` class the docstring promises requires unfolding the noncomputable `coord`.

findings.evidence: Lines 118, 131-134: both public in the `public section`; `slopeSetoid_rel_iff` used only inside `Slope.congr` (line 173).
findings.fix: Mark `slopeSetoid` and `slopeSetoid_rel_iff` `private` (drop the `@[simp]`, keeping it only as an internal `Iff.rfl` if still needed for `Slope.congr`).
findings.issue: `slopeSetoid` and `slopeSetoid_rel_iff` are public although the header (lines 87-89) declares the Quotient model an unexposed implementation detail; `slopeSetoid_rel_iff` is `@[simp]`, leaking the internal setoid relation into the global simp set. Consumers use `Slope.mk_eq_mk_iff` instead.

summary: The framing's coordinate iso is characterized forward on basis vectors but has no inverse restatement, so the advertised surgery class p·μ + q·λ is unreachable without unfolding `coord`. Separately, the internal `slopeSetoid` is over-exposed (public, with a `@[simp]` relation lemma) despite the header declaring the quotient model unexposed.
